newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sixt sees expansion giving boost to sales.
newsitem.headline: Sixt sees expansion giving boost to sales.

text.p: German car rental company Sixt AG said it planned a sweeping expansion into new markets that will send its sales and profits climbing in coming years.
Chairman Erich Sixt told a news conference that the company planned to expand into England and the Benelux countries as quickly as possible.
"We have put our antenna out," Sixt chairman Erich Sixt told a press conference, adding the company was considering expanding into countries "south of the Alps."
Expansion in England and the Benelux would give the car rental company a representation in 70 percent of the European rental car market compared with 50 percent now.
Sixt currently has operations outside Germany in France, Switzerland and Austria.
The chairman said Sixt would build up its current 310 offices mostly in smaller cities, employing less than 100 people in each location.

In its annual report also released today, Sixt said 1997 sales would improve upon last year's 2.11 billion marks and operating profits would grow at a higher than corresponding rate from 46.28 million marks.

Turnover, meanwhile, should continue to climb in the years ahead, hitting four billion marks by the year 2000 and profits should grow at about the same pace through the end of the century, the company said.

Sixt said that it would pay a 3.50 mark bonus to holders of ordinary and preferred shares. The company had already announced it would pay a 14 mark dividend on its ordinary shares and a 15 mark dividend on its preferred shares.

Hoping to broaden its shareholder base, Sixt said it would also reduce the nominal value of its shares to five marks from 50 marks a share and that it planned to convert non-voting preference shares into ordinary common stock.
The company said it would buy 68,000 vehicles this year, spending 2.2 billion marks, up from 58,000 vehicles and 1.7 billion marks last year.
The Sixt chairman, meanwhile, said he hoped the company could resolve a potentially damaging fight with its U.S. partner Budget Rent A Car Corp
The chairman said Budget is unhappy with aspects of the pair's reservation system, but that he did not expect a co-operation agreement between the two to collapse.
"We do not see a divorce," Sixt said.
